bankruptcies.description: Firms that went bankrupt this month

baseDemand.description: Units a month the market buys at basePrice

basePrice.description: Price of one unit of output when the sector produces baseDemand units a month

careerCeiling.description: Capacity firms expect an average career to approach, from their experience with their staff

cashBufferMonths.description: Months of payroll and overhead a firm wants in cash before it hires

closures.description: Firms closed this month because their owner died and nobody could buy them

comfortRunway.description: Months of living costs saved beyond which a person at work feels its savings are more than it needs

counterMargin.description: Least share of a worker's value the current employer keeps when matching an outside offer

counteroffers.description: Outside offers matched by the current employer this month

crisisMargin.description: Losses, as a share of revenue, at which a firm has no patience left with staff who cost more than they are worth; patience shrinks in proportion to losses below this

deaths.description: People who died this month for lack of income: of hunger or after months in the squeeze

elasticity.description: Price elasticity of demand: price = basePrice x (output / baseDemand)^(-1/elasticity)

entrantSavingsMonths.description: Months of living costs entrants bring on average (help from parents, student grants); each draws between half and one and a half times this

entrantsPerMonth.description: Young people entering the labor market each month, on average

entryAge.description: Age at which people enter the labor market, in months (18 years)

expectedTenure.description: Months a firm expects a new hire to stay, used to weigh what a hire earns against what it costs

fixedCost.description: Monthly overhead every firm pays whatever its size, to suppliers outside the model

foundRate.description: Monthly weight of founding a firm for an average eligible person in a sector with no profit (about 0.3% a month)

foundingShare.description: Share of its savings a founder puts into the new firm; the rest it keeps to live on

hhi.description: Herfindahl-Hirschman index of output shares (0 to 1)

hireRate.description: Most a firm can grow in a month, as a share of its headcount (recruiting capacity)

hiringCost.description: Cost of a hire (recruiting, onboarding), in months of the wage offered

horizon.description: Mean hiring horizon of the firms, in months

horizonLearn.description: Relative change of a firm's hiring horizon after one of its junior hires pays off (promoted at the firm) or fails (leaves within investmentPayback months)

hungerDeaths.description: People who died of hunger this month (not even survivalCost for food)

initialEmployment.description: Share of people employed at the start

interviewNoise.description: Standard deviation of the relative error of an interview's read of a candidate's capacity

interviewsPerOpening.description: Job seekers a firm interviews per opening

investmentPayback.description: Months a junior hire must stay for the firm to see its investment paid back

jobChanges.description: Employed people who moved to another firm this month

layoffs.description: People laid off this month, including by bankruptcy

learningRate.description: Monthly share of the distance to one's talent closed by working

additionalProperties.description: Average wage by level (junior, pleno, senior): what salary surveys publish

levelWage.description: Average wage by level (junior, pleno, senior): what salary surveys publish

lowerClass.description: Share with an income of 1 to 3 minimum wages

markdownCut.description: How much a firm raises its offers after a month with openings left unfilled, x the share unfilled

markdownRise.description: How much a firm lowers its offers (raises the markdown) after a month in which it filled all its openings

maxHorizon.description: Longest hiring horizon a firm can come to

meanWage.description: Average wage of the employed this month

middleClass.description: Share with an income of 3 to 10 minimum wages

minFoundingCapital.description: Least capital a new firm needs (about two years of an average wage)

minHires.description: Openings a firm can recruit for in a month, however small it is

minHorizon.description: Shortest hiring horizon a firm can come to

minimumWage.description: Reference minimum wage per month. Used only to classify income; it does not bind any wage

monthsShortToDie.description: Consecutive months unable to pay the full cost of living (in the squeeze, eating but cutting everything else) that kill a person

mortalityBase.description: Gompertz a: yearly chance of dying of natural causes at age 0

mortalityGrowth.description: Gompertz b: growth of the yearly risk per year of age

mpcHigh.description: Share of the wage above subsistence that people with very high pay spend

mpcLow.description: Share of the wage above subsistence that people with low pay spend

naturalDeaths.description: People who died this month of natural causes

offerLearning.description: Share of the distance between the wage a job seeker expects and the best offer it got that it revises each month

output.description: Units produced by the sector this month

overheadShare.description: Overhead that grows with the firm (rent, systems, management), as a share of its wage bill

ownerIncome.description: Mean monthly income of owners (draw and dividends, smoothed over a year)

owners.description: Share of the population that owns a firm

payoutAboveMonths.description: Profit is paid out to the owners as dividends as long as this many months of costs stay in the bank

plenoCapacity.description: Capacity at which an employer promotes a junior to pleno

poverty.description: Share of the population with an income under 1 minimum wage (unemployed included)

price.description: Price of a unit of output this month

priceAdapt.description: Share of the latest monthly price change that firms add to their expectation of the price trend

priceTrend.description: Expected monthly change of the price, from recent changes; firms value hires at the price they expect next month

profitMargin.description: Profit of the sector over its revenue last month

promotionBoost.description: Rise in job satisfaction after a promotion

quitRate.description: Weight of quitting for the most dissatisfied (satisfaction 0); falls to 0 at quitSatisfaction

quitRunway.description: Months of living costs a person wants saved before quitting without another job

quitSatisfaction.description: Job satisfaction below which a person may quit without another job

quits.description: People who quit their job this month without another one

raiseBoost.description: Rise in job satisfaction after the employer matches an outside offer

reservationDecay.description: Monthly drop of an unemployed person's lowest acceptable wage

retirementAge.description: Age at which people retire and leave the labor market, in months (65 years)

runwayComfort.description: Months of savings above which an unemployed person is not pressed to lower the wage it asks

saleProfitMonths.description: Months of profit a firm is worth, on top of its cash, when it is sold after its owner dies

satisfaction.description: Mean job satisfaction of the employed

satisfactionAdapt.description: Share of the distance to how valued it feels this month that a person's job satisfaction moves each month

satisfactionHire.description: Job satisfaction at the start of a new job (the honeymoon)

searchBase.description: Monthly weight of looking for another job for an employed person paid like its peers

searchDissatisfaction.description: Extra weight of looking for another job per unit of job satisfaction below 0.5

searchGap.description: Extra weight of looking for another job per unit of pay shortfall against the peers' average wage

additionalProperties.description: This month's job seekers, by agent id: the lowest wage each accepts. Only the market reads it

seeking.description: This month's job seekers, by agent id: the lowest wage each accepts. Only the market reads it

seniorCapacity.description: Capacity at which an employer promotes a pleno to senior

seniors.description: Share of the labor force at the senior level

shrinkInterviews.description: Recruiters distrust extreme interview reads and pull them toward the average of the candidates, in proportion to how unreliable interviews are

skillDecay.description: Monthly share of capacity lost while unemployed

squeezed.description: Share of the labor force in the squeeze: unable to pay the full cost of living this month

startupMonths.description: Months a new firm may hire before it has to be profitable to keep hiring

subsistence.description: Cost of living per month: basic food and housing

survivalCost.description: Least money a month for food. An unemployed person who starts a month without it, after a first month of grace, dies of hunger

switchPremium.description: Raise an employed worker requires to move to another firm

timePreference.description: Mean time preference of the labor force

timePreferenceDrift.description: How much a month at work with savings beyond comfortRunway raises a person's time preference: savings it never needs feel less necessary

timePreferenceLearn.description: How much a month of hardship (unemployed, or unable to pay the full cost of living) lowers a person's time preference: it learns that savings matter

timePreferenceSpend.description: How much more of the wage above subsistence the most present-minded spend than the average person, and the least spend less

unemployment.description: Share of the people who are not owners without a job

upperClass.description: Share with an income above 10 minimum wages

wealthSpending.description: Share of savings spent each month (about 5% a year): consumption out of wealth
